newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lernout to launch voice-operated phone.
newsitem.headline: Lernout to launch voice-operated phone.

text.p: Nasdaq-listed Belgian technology firm Lernout & Hauspie (L&H) said on Friday its new voice-operated calling and answering module for cellular telephones would be introduced around the third quarter 1997.
Based on L&H's speech recognition technology and the small hardware design of Belgian technology company Cardian, the module offered voice-activated, hands-free dialling.

"L&H expects the module to experience its greatest acceptance in the automotive industry, where safety, convenience and efficiency improve with a cellular phone that understands basic verbal commands, such as 'call the office' or 'get my messages'," the company said in a statement.
It added that, when combined with desktop messaging software, the cellular telephone would allow users to retrieve e-mail messages when they were on the road by using voice commands.
The module will be sold to original equipment manufacturers, who will sell it under their own brand names. L&H will also sell it directly in some markets.

L&H is also planning to launch an automatic translation service for the Internet by the end of the year, after winning a $35 million contract from the Brussels Translation Consortium, a private fund, to develop such a service.
